name: s12-offsets
title: Picturing offsets
spec: A string S = 'spam' drawn as four cells. Above the cells forward offsets 0 1 2 3, below them backward offsets -4 -3 -2 -1. A bracket under cells 1 and 2 labelled S[1:3] gives 'pa'. Three small chips on the right: S[0] gives 's' ; S[-1] gives 'm' ; S[:2] gives 'sp'. Orange note: the stop offset is not included.
cap: Offsets count forward from 0 and backward from -1, and a slice stops before its end offset.

name: s12-copies
title: Shallow versus deep copy
spec: Left panel Shallow copy: two outer lists L and M = L.copy(), each with an arrow to the same inner list [2, 3] (orange, shared), caption changing the inner list shows up in both. Right panel Deep copy: L and N = copy.deepcopy(L) with separate inner lists (green), caption fully independent.
cap: A shallow copy shares the inner objects, while a deep copy duplicates them.

name: s12-exactnums
title: Binary floats versus exact numbers
spec: Three rows. Row float: 0.1 + 0.1 + 0.1 == 0.3 is False (orange, binary approximation). Row Decimal: Decimal('0.1') * 3 == Decimal('0.3') is True (green, exact decimal digits). Row Fraction: Fraction(1, 3) stays exact, no rounding. Bottom bar: pick the numeric type to match the accuracy you need.
cap: float is a binary approximation, while Decimal and Fraction keep exact values.

name: s12-fmt
title: Four ways to format a string
spec: Four rows, each a code chip on the left and the same result chip node1 is up on the right. Rows: f-string f"{name} is up" ; format method "{} is up".format(name) ; percent expression "%s is up" % name ; string.Template Template("$name is up").substitute(name=name). Orange highlight on the f-string row.
cap: Four formatting tools produce the same text, and f-strings are the most direct.

name: s12-filemodes
title: File open modes
spec: A table: mode letters as green chips with a meaning. r read (the default) ; w write, truncates the file first (orange) ; a append at the end ; b binary, bytes instead of text ; + read and write ; t text, the default. Under it a code chip: open('log.txt', 'a', encoding='utf-8') with pointers to the file name, the mode and the encoding.
cap: The open() mode letters choose reading, writing, appending, and text or binary.
